SB_Theme_CoOccurrence: Within-paper co-emphasis correlation of the ten spaceflight-risk themes across the on-target literature (n=4,415) — which risks are studied together.
SB_Theme_Network: Force-directed theme co-occurrence network; greedy-modularity communities with nodes coloured by 30-year momentum — the falling human-physiology risks form one connected community.
SB_Momentum_Acceleration: Acceleration map: each theme's early (1995–99→2015–19) vs recent (2015–19→2020–24) emphasis momentum — is the drift speeding up or slowing?
SB_Trajectories_Annotated: Five representative emphasis trajectories (1995–2024) annotated with the real-world programmes, facilities and landmark publications that drove them.
SB_Sequencing_Omics: Omics & microbiome literature emphasis against NHGRI cost-per-genome (log, inverted) — the molecular turn as an exogenous, sequencing-cost-driven tide.
Topics: After filtering csvs with high semantic similarity to "unknown/to be researched", we developed a profile on what is considered important to research.
SB_Frontier_Map: Intertopic distance map of the 10,499 literature papers that explicitly acknowledge an unknown (72 topics, HDBSCAN min_cluster_size 20 / min_samples 4 on the existing 5-D coords) — a documented rebuild of the Topics.html method, in the same projection as SB_Distance_Map.
Frontier_Density: Share of each of the four corpora whose passages carry an explicit acknowledged-unknown cue. Funded proposals 22.9% > Decadal 9.9% ≈ Literature 9.2% > OSDR 5.3% — a finding about genre, not intellectual honesty.
Frontier_Retrieval: AUC for retrieving passages containing an explicit hedge, by scoring method. SPECTER2 semantic scoring barely beats chance on abstracts (0.581) and hybrid RRF (0.661) lands BELOW keyword alone (0.742): embeddings encode topic, not epistemic stance.
Frontier_Openness_4way: Per-theme openness lift — open-question rate among each corpus's most theme-leaning quarter minus its own baseline — across all four windows. Omics is the most-flagged theme in three of four; plant/crops the least-flagged in the literature.
Frontier_vs_Momentum: Literature openness lift against 30-year emphasis momentum (r = −0.42): the field admits ignorance about the risks it is abandoning and stays quiet about the ones it is racing toward. SANS is the falling-and-unflagged outlier.
Frontier_vs_Funded: Literature openness lift against funded emphasis (r = +0.54) — NASA's money is aimed at the themes the literature itself calls open, a third independent route to the finding that the funded portfolio is better-aimed than the published field.
